title: DIO/ODI Semantic Change Feed
description: A curated, append-only record covering the complete DIO/ODI Hub Changelog from 25 March to 25 October 2026, together with subsequently documented vocabulary, mapping, publication, research-portfolio, and Reference Model release events through 9 November 2026.

policy.correction_rule: Corrections are new events linked to earlier records; published event records are not silently overwritten.

events.title: Initial work on the text exposes a latent semantic space
events.summary: The Changelog records the start of work on the professional-ethnography text and the emergence of a previously unnamed latent space. This is the project-origin milestone, not yet the formal naming of DIO.
events.before: The work had not yet been explicitly articulated as DIO/ODI.
events.after: A latent semantic space is recorded as having emerged during the writing process.
preserved_invariants: This date marks the beginning of the documented writing process, not the formal articulation of DIO.

impact.notes: Project-origin milestone; it records the start of the documented writing process and the emergence of a latent semantic space, not a fully specified theoretical proposition.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: Digital Identity Optimization is articulated
events.summary: The Changelog identifies 21 May as the point at which a newly recognized dimension and possibility for optimizing and viewing digital identity was articulated as Digital Identity Optimization.
events.before: The latent space had been recognized but did not yet have the DIO designation.
events.after: The concept is explicitly articulated as Digital Identity Optimization (DIO).
preserved_invariants: This records the Changelog's stated articulation date; it does not claim that every later DIO construct was already defined.

impact.notes: Initial articulation of DIO; later publications refine and formalize the framework.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: The first Czech Manifest is published
events.summary: The first Czech-language version of the DIO/ODI Manifest is published.
events.before: DIO had been articulated, but the first Manifest version had not yet been published.
events.after: A first Czech Manifest publication provides a documented textual formulation of DIO.
preserved_invariants: The first Czech publication is distinct from the later canonical multilingual Zenodo edition.

impact.notes: The Changelog date refers to publication of the first Czech version; the multilingual archive follows on 27 July.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: Ontology of Digital Identity is articulated as a broader theoretical layer
events.summary: The Changelog records the articulation of a more general theoretical level, distinguished from DIO's applied optimization focus, as Ontology of Digital Identity (ODI).
events.before: DIO was framed around practical optimization of digital identity.
events.after: ODI is articulated as the broader theoretical layer concerned with digital identity and its conditions of being.
preserved_invariants: DIO's applied orientation and ODI's broader theoretical scope are distinguished rather than collapsed.

impact.notes: The record captures the Changelog's conceptual distinction; later scoping and methodological notes elaborate it.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: The Manifest is projected into fifteen additional languages
events.summary: Fifteen additional language projections are created between 15 and 26 July, extending the Czech source into a coordinated multilingual set.
events.before: The Manifest existed as a Czech-language source.
events.after: Fifteen additional language projections are created, producing a sixteen-language corpus.
preserved_invariants: Language projections are coordinated representations; they do not constitute sixteen independent theories.

impact.notes: The Changelog provides the interval 15–26 July; it does not assign a separate completion date to each language.

evidence.temporal_note: The Changelog gives a bounded activity period, not a single publication or edit timestamp.

events.title: Sixteen language versions are consolidated at one hub
events.summary: The sixteen language versions are brought together at a single nodal point for language projections.
events.before: Language versions were distributed across separate representations.
events.after: A single web hub makes the sixteen language projections jointly discoverable.
preserved_invariants: Consolidation at the hub does not make the language versions identical strings or remove their autonomous linguistic projections.

impact.notes: A distribution and discoverability change, not a conceptual revision.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.after: A public-facing product page and explicit Changelog are created.
preserved_invariants: The Changelog is a retrospective, author-maintained record and must be distinguished from source-control history.

events.title: Manifest v2 introduces the Semantic Connectome visualization and semantic-field analogy
events.summary: The Czech and English Manifest v2 editions add a visualization of the Semantic Connectome as a complete graph K6 and interpret its relational structure through the working analogy of a semantic field. The Changelog also records a shift away from linear or sequential readings toward simultaneous interaction.

scope.component: Manifest v2 — semantic connectome and semantic-field analogy

events.before: The earlier Manifest representation did not yet include the v2 connectome visualization and its interpretive supplement.
events.after: The Semantic Connectome is visualized as a complete graph K6 and supplemented by a working analogy of a semantic field; the account rejects a linear or sequential reading of the invariant and methodology.
preserved_invariants: The semantic-field analogy is identified as a working analogy, not a physical field or an asserted mathematical proof.
K6 names the explicit graph-theoretic representation (the complete graph on six vertices), not the general Semantic Connectome concept.

The 20 August 2026 Czech and English Manifest v2 web editions are a living web publication, not a new Zenodo archive; the canonical multilingual Zenodo record dated 27 July 2026 remains the archived v1.0.0 edition.

affected_components: Manifest v2 — semantic connectome and semantic-field analogy
impact.notes: The Changelog specifies Czech and English v2 editions; it does not assert that every language edition changed on this date.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp. events.after: The Crisis paper publishes an initial four-part anomaly framing for Entity Resolution.
preserved_invariants: The four-item Crisis framing is a historical state; later publications refine the classification and separate Semantic Vulnerability from realized failure modes.

impact.notes: The paper publishes an initial four-part anomaly framing. This is the historical starting classification; later publications refine it and separate Semantic Vulnerability from realized failure modes.

events.title: MVDIO introduces adversarial reduction and clarifies its relationship to the Semantic Connectome
events.summary: MVDIO reduces DIO to a minimum analytical model, refines reconstruction-failure distinctions, reclassifies Semantic Vulnerability toward robustness/risk, and clarifies the relation between its coarse-grained minimum and the finer-grained Semantic Connectome.
events.before: The Crisis-era account used a four-anomaly framing and had not yet made the relation between MVDIO's minimum analytical model and the Semantic Connectome explicit.
events.after: MVDIO provides an adversarially reduced analytical model and clarifies the relationship between its coarse-grained minimum and the finer-grained Semantic Connectome, while moving Semantic Vulnerability toward robustness/risk.
preserved_invariants: The Semantic Connectome is treated as a finer-grained candidate model, not as a logical consequence of MVDIO.

impact.notes: This event captures the compound conceptual development as described in the MVDIO Changelog entry.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: The Taxonomic Note reorganizes anomalies into Reconstruction Failure Modes
events.summary: The Taxonomic Note reorganizes the original Entity Resolution Anomalies into a multi-level diagnostic taxonomy with Referential Reconstruction, Semantic Coherence, Temporal Reconstruction, and Contextual Adequacy branches.
events.before: The initial Crisis paper used a four-anomaly framing.
events.after: A multi-level Reconstruction Failure Modes taxonomy is published; Identity Collapse remains outside it and Semantic Vulnerability is treated as a robustness-related property rather than a realized failure mode.
preserved_invariants: The taxonomy remains distinct from Identity Collapse.
Semantic Vulnerability is not classified as a realized failure mode.

impact.notes: This is the formal taxonomic revision, not merely a visualization update.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: Constraining the Commit Boundary introduces a DIO/ODI-informed authorization guardrail
events.summary: The paper develops a conceptual architecture for authorization of persistent identity changes in Agentic Entity Resolution, separating evidence available for agent reasoning from evidence eligible to authorize a specific identity or continuity claim.
events.before: DIO/ODI had application mappings for RAG and HEM but had not yet published this commit-boundary authorization architecture.
events.after: A commit-time authorization guardrail is specified with operational scope and current state/policy conditions.
preserved_invariants: The paper is a conceptual architecture; publication does not imply implementation, formal proof, or empirical validation.

impact.notes: The wider hypothesis-conditioned agentic cascade is explicitly left as future research.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is transcribed from the author-maintained DIO/ODI Hub Changelog; it is not automatically asserted as a Git commit timestamp.

events.title: Agentic ER Architecture Mapping v0.3.0 formalizes the Commit-Boundary architecture
events.summary: The first archived version of the DIO/ODI-informed Agentic Entity Resolution Commit-Boundary Architecture Mapping formalizes the architecture's internal conceptual and functional relations in a derived, non-normative layer. The v0.3.0 snapshot contains 120 local architecture concepts and 206 qualified relation assertions and is included in Reference Model v0.6.0.
events.before: The Commit-Boundary paper had proposed the authorization guardrail, but the coordinated machine-readable relational mapping had not yet appeared in an archived Reference Model package.
events.after: Mapping v0.3.0 provides the first archived formalization of the paper's internal conceptual and functional relations and is included in Reference Model v0.6.0.
preserved_invariants: The mapping is derived and non-normative; it does not modify the canonical Reference Vocabulary.
Its 120 local concepts and 206 qualified relations describe the paper-specific architecture rather than adding canonical DIO/ODI concepts.
The existence of the mapping does not establish implementation, formal proof, or empirical validation.

impact.notes: This records the first archival inclusion of the mapping. Its metadata declares a creation date of 3 November 2026; the exact source-edit timestamp is not asserted.

evidence.temporal_note: Date marks first public archival inclusion in Reference Model v0.6.0 on 5 November. The archived v0.6.0 mapping JSON-LD separately declares schema:dateCreated as 3 November 2026; the date of first inclusion is not treated as the exact creation timestamp.

events.title: The DIO-to-DIO research portfolio publishes ten model-specific reconstruction analyses
events.summary: The public DIO to DIO portfolio brings together ten author-led analyses of how different LLMs reconstruct and examine the DIO/ODI ecosystem. The reports retain model-specific observation boundaries, interpretations, graph models, and conclusions; the portfolio does not harmonize, rank, or synthesize them. The public site exposes the original Markdown and PDF reports alongside generated HTML representations.
events.before: The analyses existed as individually produced model-specific research reports but had not yet been published together through a common public portfolio.
events.after: Ten reports by Brave AI, ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Gemini Deep Research, Gemini Pro Latest, Leo AI, Lumo, Mistral, Qwen, and Grok are available through a common public catalogue.
preserved_invariants: The project is author-led: the author defines and directs the research; the models contribute distinct analytical readings.
The reports are not harmonized, ranked, or synthesized; their observation boundaries, graph approaches, and conclusions remain report-specific.
The public deployment date is not treated as the generation or observation date of every report; the catalogue retains each report's own observation snapshot.
The portfolio does not modify the canonical Reference Vocabulary or validate the historical claims made in an individual report.

impact.notes: This is a public research and distribution milestone. Individual model analyses are treated as discovery and interpretation sources; historical claims adopted by the SCF must be verified against primary publications, registries, release records, or archives.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is the successful public GitHub Pages deployment date (6 November 2026). Individual reports have their own observation snapshots, mostly 30 October 2026 and, for Grok, early November; those dates are not replaced by the portfolio publication date.

sources.label: DIO to DIO — successful Pages deployment

events.title: The DIO-to-DIO portfolio adds its eleventh model-specific analysis by Claude Sonnet
events.summary: The public portfolio expands from ten to eleven author-led analyses with Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Extra Effort). The report examines reconstruction resilience across web, archival, machine-readable, multilingual, and identity-linked representations. Its section on strains and materiality distinguishes structural susceptibilities and documented state differences from demonstrated reconstruction failures; these remain Claude's model-specific analytical findings, not harmonized portfolio conclusions or authoritative historical evidence.
events.before: The public portfolio contained ten author-led, model-specific reconstruction analyses, as recorded at its initial publication milestone in SCF-2026-042.
events.after: Eleven analyses are publicly available. The Claude Sonnet 5.5 report is listed with its Markdown and PDF source files and a generated HTML representation; its observation snapshot is 6–7 November 2026.
preserved_invariants: SCF-2026-042 remains the accurate record of the portfolio's initial publication with ten analyses on 6 November 2026; this event appends the subsequent expansion and does not rewrite that history.
The portfolio remains author-led: the author defines and directs the research, while each model contributes a distinct analytical reading.
The reports remain model-specific and are not harmonized, ranked, or synthesized; Claude's materiality judgments and graph results are not promoted to portfolio-wide conclusions.
The report's observation snapshot (6–7 November 2026) is distinct from the portfolio publication/deployment date (7 November 2026).

The report's observations are discovery and interpretation material, not primary historical authority; claims adopted as SCF history require verification against primary publications, registries, release records, or archives.
The portfolio addition does not modify the canonical Reference Vocabulary, Application Mappings, or archived Reference Model releases.

impact.notes: This is a portfolio distribution update. The report's section 8 provides a model-specific, task-relative materiality assessment and explicitly reports no established realized reconstruction failure or measured observer outcome within its inspected evidence.

evidence.temporal_note: Date is the successful GitHub Pages deployment on 7 November 2026 (workflow run 42414438200). The Claude report records an observation snapshot of 6–7 November 2026; that snapshot is not used as the portfolio publication date.

sources.label: Claude analysis — HTML report, section 8: Strains and their materiality
DIO to DIO — successful Pages deployment, 7 November 2026

events.summary: The preferred compact namespace prefix changes from dio to dio-odi and is synchronized across the canonical Turtle, JSON-LD, embedded HTML graph, derived Application Mapping Turtle serializations, and SPARQL examples. The namespace URI and all 40 concept URIs remain unchanged.

events.after: Reference Vocabulary v0.2.2 declares dio-odi as its preferred namespace prefix and uses dio-odi: consistently across those representations. The canonical namespace URI and all local concept identifiers remain unchanged.
preserved_invariants: The canonical namespace URI https://vocab.danielberanek.cz/dio-odi/# is unchanged.
The canonical ConceptScheme URI and all 40 SKOS concept URIs are unchanged.
Concept labels, definitions, notes, hierarchy, provenance, and the semantics of derived Application Mappings are unchanged.
The archived Reference Model v0.8.0 remains an immutable snapshot containing Reference Vocabulary v0.2.1.

impact.notes: This is a namespace-prefix metadata and serialization update only. It does not change concept identity, concept semantics, graph relations, or the meaning of any derived mapping. The current archived Reference Model v0.8.0 remains unchanged.

evidence.temporal_note: The date is the recorded publication date of Reference Vocabulary v0.2.2 in its release notes. It is not a Hub Changelog date and does not imply a concept-model change.
